alternatives: Prospective audit of new airway events from now on (refused: cannot show change since 2023 and takes years to accrue events)
Simple before-after comparison of two periods (refused: ignores the pre-existing trend and co-interventions)
Survey of anaesthetists about alerts (refused as the main design: measures opinion, not recognition)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled design across hospitals is not possible because other hospitals' records are not accessible; a segmented series within the hospital is the strongest feasible design.
rationale: The before-after wristband study behind claim c1 no longer counts as support: its identifier resolved to a different work. The design question is unchanged, and the remaining retrieved evidence still supports a retrospective segmented series: display is not recognition (claim c2), unanticipated difficulty is common (claim c3) and database capture must be reported (claim c4). Planning values for recognition come from the hospital's own pre-change data instead of claim c1.

decision.statement: Conduct the retrospective segmented time series of documented recognition before later airway management from the database and anaesthetic records, with planning values taken from the hospital's own pre-change data and database capture reported alongside every outcome.
decision.question: How should the hospital evaluate its difficult airway alert system now that one supporting record has been found to be misattributed?

criteria.text: Display is not recognition and unanticipated difficulty is common, so a local measure of recognition would inform the committee.
Database capture is too low to support outcome estimates.
